```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(reshape2)

# Your data (replace with your actual data)
data <- data.frame(
  Trait = c("SLA", "LDMC", "C:N", "C", "P", 
            "SLA", "LDMC", "C:N", "C", "P", 
            "SLA", "LDMC", "C:N", "C", "P"),
  Model = factor(c(rep("PLSR", 5), rep("RF", 5), rep("CNN", 5)), levels = c("PLSR", "RF", "CNN")),
  Type = rep("Training", 15),
  R2 = c(0.89, 0.85, 0.72, 0.68, 0.66, 
         0.87, 0.54, 0.57, 0.37, 0.50, 
         0.88, 0.85, 0.59, 0.46, 0.52)
)

data_melted <- melt(data, id.vars = c("Trait", "Model", "Type"), measure.vars = "R2", value.name = "R2")

ggplot(data_melted, aes(x = Model, y = Trait, fill = R2)) +
  geom_tile() +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high = "darkblue") +  # Adjust colors as needed
  labs(title = "Comparing R-squared Values", x = "Model", y = "Trait", fill = "R-squared") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

```


```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(ggthemes)  # For modern themes

# Your data
data <- data.frame(
  Trait = c("SLA", "LDMC", "C:N", "C", "P", "SLA (H 30%)", "SLA (L 30%)", "SLA", "LDMC", "C:N", "C", "P", "SLA (H 30%)", "SLA (L 30%)", "SLA", "LDMC", "C:N", "C", "P"),
  Model = factor(c(rep("PLSR", 7), rep("RF", 7), rep("CNN", 5)), levels = c("PLSR", "RF", "CNN")),
  Type = c(rep("Training", 5), rep("Extrapolation", 2), rep("Training", 5), rep("Extrapolation", 2), rep("Training", 5)),
  R2 = c(0.89, 0.85, 0.72, 0.68, 0.66, 0.26, 0.27, 0.87, 0.54, 0.57, 0.37, 0.50, 0.05, 0.08, 0.88, 0.85, 0.59, 0.46, 0.52),
  RMSE = c(0.40, 0.41, 0.50, 0.55, 0.64, 1.02, 0.41, 0.42, 0.72, 0.63, 0.82, 0.66, 1.29, 0.74, 0.39, 0.35, 0.60, 0.70, 0.70)
)

# Filter out extrapolation data
data <- subset(data, Type == "Training")  # Keep only "Training" rows

j1 <- ggplot(data, aes(x = Model, y = R2, fill = Model)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(title = "R-squared Distribution by Model", x = "Model", y = "R-squared") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#0072B5", "#D55E00", "#009E73")) + # Modern color palette
  theme_bw() +
  facet_wrap(~Type) # Facet by Training/Extrapolation

# Repeat the above for RMSE
j2 <- ggplot(data, aes(x = Model, y = RMSE, fill = Model)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(title = "RMSE Distribution by Model", x = "Model", y = "RMSE") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#0072B5", "#D55E00", "#009E73")) + # Modern color palette
  theme_bw() +
  facet_wrap(~Type) # Facet by Training/Extrapolation

ggplotly(j1)
ggplotly(j2)
```


```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

# Your data (as provided)
data <- data.frame(
  Trait = c("SLA", "LDMC", "C:N", "C", "P", "SLA (H 30%)", "SLA (L 30%)", "SLA", "LDMC", "C:N", "C", "P", "SLA (H 30%)", "SLA (L 30%)", "SLA", "LDMC", "C:N", "C", "P"),
  Model = factor(c(rep("PLSR", 7), rep("RF", 7), rep("CNN", 5)), levels = c("PLSR", "RF", "CNN")),
  Type = c(rep("Training", 5), rep("Extrapolation", 2), rep("Training", 5), rep("Extrapolation", 2), rep("Training", 5)),
  R2 = c(0.89, 0.85, 0.72, 0.68, 0.66, 0.26, 0.27, 0.87, 0.54, 0.57, 0.37, 0.50, 0.05, 0.08, 0.88, 0.85, 0.59, 0.46, 0.52),
  RMSE = c(0.40, 0.41, 0.50, 0.55, 0.64, 1.02, 0.41, 0.42, 0.72, 0.63, 0.82, 0.66, 1.29, 0.74, 0.39, 0.35, 0.60, 0.70, 0.70)
)

# Filter out extrapolation data
data_training <- data %>% filter(Type == "Training")
f3 <- ggplot(data_training, aes(x = RMSE, y = R2, shape = Model, color = Model, fill = Model)) +  # Added fill = Model
  geom_point(size = 3, stroke = 1) +  # Added stroke for better visibility
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(21, 22, 23)) + # Different shapes for each model
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("PLSR" = "darkblue", "RF" = "darkred", "CNN" = "darkgreen")) + #added color to fill
  scale_color_manual(values = c("PLSR" = "darkblue", "RF" = "darkred", "CNN" = "darkgreen")) + #added color to border
  theme_minimal() +
    theme(panel.grid.major = element_blank(), #Remove grid lines
          panel.border = element_blank(),
          panel.background = element_blank(),
          axis.ticks = element_blank()) +
  labs(title = "Scatter Plot of R² vs. RMSE", x = "RMSE", y = "R²")

print(f3)
```


```{r}

data <- data.frame(
  Trait = c("SLA", "LDMC", "C:N", "C", "P", "SLA (H 30%)", "SLA (L 30%)", "SLA", "LDMC", "C:N", "C", "P", "SLA (H 30%)", "SLA (L 30%)", "SLA", "LDMC", "C:N", "C", "P", "SLA (H 30%)", "SLA (L 30%)" ),
  Model = factor(c(rep("PLSR", 7), rep("RF", 7), rep("CNN", 7)), levels = c("PLSR", "RF", "CNN")), # Important for ordering
  Type = c(rep("Training", 5), rep("Extrapolation", 2), rep("Training", 5), rep("Extrapolation", 2), rep("Training", 5), rep("Extrapolation", 2)),
  R2 = c(0.89, 0.85, 0.72, 0.68, 0.66, 0.26, 0.27, 0.87, 0.54, 0.57, 0.37, 0.50, 0.05, 0.08, 0.88, 0.85, 0.59, 0.46, 0.52, 0.22, 0.31),
  RMSE = c(0.40, 0.41, 0.50, 0.55, 0.64, 1.02, 0.41, 0.42, 0.72, 0.63, 0.82, 0.66, 1.29, 0.74, 0.39, 0.35, 0.60, 0.70, 0.70, 0.66, 0.65)
)
# Your data (add training time to the data frame)
data$Training_Time <- c(13.76, 11.40, 15.71, 13.63, 15.19, 14.18, 12.91, 12.85*60, 12.11*60, 12.60*60, 13.17*60, 15.25*60, 11.78*60, 11.98*60, 8.84*60, 6.01*60, 4.02*60, 5.07*60, 30.78, 6.46*60, 3.20*60) # in seconds, convert minutes to seconds for RF and CNN

ggplot(data, aes(x = Training_Time, y = R2, color = Model, shape=Type)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  labs(title = "R-squared vs. Training Time", x = "Training Time (seconds)", y = "R-squared", color = "Model", shape="Type") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("darkblue", "darkgreen", "darkred")) + # Customize colors
  theme_bw() +
  scale_x_log10() # Use log scale if training times vary greatly
```


```{r}
library(plotly)
library(dplyr)

# Filter out extrapolation data
data_filtered <- data %>%
  filter(Type == "Training") %>%
  mutate(Training_Time_min = Training_Time / 60)  # Convert time to minutes for readability

# Create the 3D scatter plot
fig <- plot_ly(data_filtered, 
               x = ~Training_Time_min, 
               y = ~R2, 
               z = ~Model, 
               type = "scatter3d", 
               mode = "markers", 
               marker = list(size = 6, color = ~as.numeric(as.factor(Model)), colorscale = "Viridis")) 

# Add labels and layout
fig <- fig %>% layout(
  title = "3D Plot: R² vs Training Time across Models",
  scene = list(
    xaxis = list(title = "Training Time (min)"),
    yaxis = list(title = "R²"),
    zaxis = list(title = "Model")
  )
)

# Show plot
fig



```


```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)


# Convert training time to minutes and remove extrapolation data
data_filtered <- data %>%
  filter(Type == "Training") %>%
  mutate(Training_Time_min = Training_Time / 60)  # Convert seconds to minutes

# Create the heatmap
ggplot(data_filtered, aes(x = Model, y = Trait, fill = Training_Time_min)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = round(Training_Time_min, 1)), color = "black", size = 4) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "lightblue", high = "darkblue", name = "Training Time (min)") +
  labs(title = "Heatmap of Training Time Across Models and Traits",
       x = "Model",
       y = "Trait") +
  theme_minimal()


```



```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

# Filter out extrapolation data
filtered_data <- data %>%
  filter(Type == "Training")

# Create the ggplot
ggplot(filtered_data, aes(x = R2, y = Model, color = Trait, group = Trait)) +
  geom_point(size = 4) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Comparing the predictive accuracy of ML models using R-square value", 
       x = expression(R^2), 
       y = "Model",
       color = "Trait") +
  theme(legend.position = "right")

```

####### Plotting the effect of dimensionality reduction

```{r}
# Original results (2151 features)

data1 <- data.frame(
  Trait = c("SLA", "LDMC", "C:N", "C", "P", "SLA (H 30%)", "SLA (L 30%)", "SLA", "LDMC", "C:N", "C", "P", "SLA (H 30%)", "SLA (L 30%)", "SLA", "LDMC", "C:N", "C", "P", "SLA (H 30%)", "SLA (L 30%)" ),
  Model = factor(c(rep("PLSR", 7), rep("RF", 7), rep("CNN", 7)), levels = c("PLSR", "RF", "CNN")), # Important for ordering
  Type = c(rep("Training", 5), rep("Extrapolation", 2), rep("Training", 5), rep("Extrapolation", 2), rep("Training", 5), rep("Extrapolation", 2)),
  R2 = c(0.89, 0.85, 0.72, 0.68, 0.66, 0.26, 0.27, 0.87, 0.54, 0.57, 0.37, 0.50, 0.05, 0.08, 0.88, 0.85, 0.59, 0.46, 0.52, 0.22, 0.31),
  RMSE = c(0.40, 0.41, 0.50, 0.55, 0.64, 1.02, 0.41, 0.42, 0.72, 0.63, 0.82, 0.66, 1.29, 0.74, 0.39, 0.35, 0.60, 0.70, 0.70, 0.66, 0.65)
)

# Feature engineered data
data2 <- data.frame(
  Trait = c("SLA", "LDMC", "C:N", "C", "P", "SLA", "LDMC", "C:N", "C", "P",  "SLA", "LDMC", "C:N", "C", "P" ),
  Model = factor(c(rep("PLSR", 5), rep("RF", 5), rep("CNN", 5)), levels = c("PLSR", "RF", "CNN")), # Important for ordering
  Type = c(rep("Training", 5), rep("Training", 5), rep("Training", 5)),

  R2 = c(0.90, 0.82,0.76,0.63,0.69,0.86,0.74,0.60,0.58,0.68,0.88,0.86,0.69,0.64,0.66),
  RMSE = c(0.37,0.44,0.48,0.68,0.60,0.44,0.55,0.59,0.67,0.59,0.43,0.45,0.78,0.66,0.52)
)



library(ggplot2)

# Remove extrapolation values from data1
data1 <- data1 %>% filter(Type == "Training")

# Combine both datasets with a new column to identify them
data1$Dataset <- "Feature Engineered"
data2$Dataset <- "Original Features"
combined_data <- rbind(data1, data2)

# Plot
ggplot(combined_data, aes(x = RMSE, y = R2, color = Trait, shape = Dataset)) +
  geom_point(size = 4) +
  labs(title = "Effect of Dimensionality Reduction on ML Model Performance",
       x = "RMSE",
       y = "R²") +
  theme_minimal() +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(16, 17))  # Different shapes for datasets



```

## Plots of LCMS 

# PLSR
```{r}
plsr <- read.csv("/Users/methungeorge/Desktop/Master-Thesis-IPB-THD-/outputs/PLSR_Results_LCMS.csv")

r2_data_plsr <- plsr[, c(1,2)]

# Load required library
library(ggplot2)

# Overlayed plot
p1 <- ggplot(r2_data_plsr, aes(x = factor(1), y = R2)) +
  # Violin plot
  geom_violin(fill = "#87BB62", color = "black", outlier.color = "red", trim = FALSE) +
  # Boxplot overlayed
  geom_boxplot(fill = "#1f77b4", color = "black", outlier.color = "red", width = 0.2) +
  labs(title = "Violin and Boxplot of R² Distribution (PLSR)", 
       y = "R² Value", 
       x = "") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.title.x = element_blank(),
        axis.text.x = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
        plot.title = element_text(size = 12),
        axis.title.y = element_text(size = 10),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10)) 


p1
#

```
